items.title: AI Shell: An Intent-Aware, Secure, and Iterative Natural Language Interface for System Commands
items.abstract: Command-line interfaces remain essential for system administration and development workflows, yet require mastery of complex syntax that creates barriers for novice users. This paper presents AI Shell, a production-ready natural language command interface powered by Google's Gemini API that enables users to generate, refine, and execute shell commands through conversational interaction. The system implements intent-aware processing to distinguish between command generation, email composition, and interactive chat; filesystem context awareness providing LLM access to current directory state; multi-step execution planning with user verification at each stage; PIN-based security authentication for high-risk operations including deletions and system modifications; and SMTP email integration with iterative draft refinement. Practical evaluation across comprehensive command categories demonstrates successful execution of file operations, network diagnostics, git workflows, system administration tasks, and email composition. The architecture uses JSON-based configuration, direct shell execution with error handling, and streaming LLM responses for real-time interaction. Key contributions include: (1) iterative command refinement workflow allowing users to edit, revise, or regenerate commands before execution, (2) risk classification system with password protection for dangerous operations, (3) filesystem-aware prompting improving command accuracy for location-dependent tasks, (4) email workflow with multi-turn clarification and draft improvement, and (5) cross-platform shell compatibility supporting bash, zsh, fish, and PowerShell.

items.title: AI Technologies and Economic Transformation: A Systematic Review Comparing Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and Generative Models
items.abstract: Technologies based on Artificial Intelligence (AI) are transforming the economic framework of the world into a more data-optimized system with autonomous decision intelligence and generative innovation. In this paper, the systematic review of modern literature comparing the economic transformation impact of Machine Learning (ML), Deep learning (DL), and Generative AI models will be provided. In contrast to the solitary technological examinations, this one assumes the evolutionary point of view, which sees the development of AI in three phases: predictive optimization (ML), intelligent automation (DL), and generative cognitive augmentation (Generative AI). Peer-reviewed journal articles that were indexed in the Scopus and SCI databases were systematically reviewed to estimate sectoral, macroeconomic, and labor market effects. The results suggest that ML mainly boosts productivity by increasing the predictive efficiency, DL hastens automation and capital deepening in high-skill industries, and Generative AI brings innovative disruption with profound effects on the structure of employment, knowledge-based ecosystems, and high-skill industries. The comparative evaluation shows some level of differences in scale, patterns of substituting labor, explainability, and economic inclusiveness. Moreover, as new findings reveal, Generative AI can transform the value generation by enriching cognitive work instead of automation of habitual processes. The paper suggests an evolutionary framework of AI-Economy transformation to generalize these results and point out the further research in the directions of governance, sustainability, and inclusive growth. The review will add to the emergent interdisciplinary debate on AI-based economic change by providing a comparable model of comparison that can be used by policy, industry, and academic researchers.

items.abstract: The advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming Library and Information Science (LIS) education globally, with strong implications for Nigeria. This chapter explores AI trends and their intersection with entrepreneurial leadership as a framework for repositioning LIS education in the digital era. AI tools such as natural language processing, machine learning, intelligent tutoring, predictive analytics, and virtual reference services are redefining curricula, pedagogy, research, and professional practice, enabling personalized learning, market-responsive programs, and greater research productivity. In Nigeria, entrepreneurial leadership driven by foresight, flexibility, and innovation is vital to bridge gaps between technology and institutional transformation. Challenges such as poor funding, infrastructural deficits, and undervaluation of LIS persist. The chapter recommends curriculum reform, training, mentorship, and partnerships to embed digital skills, boost employability, and align LIS education with the global economy, AU Agenda 2063, and SDG 4.

items.title: AI-Agri shield: Blockchain-Based Crop Index Insurance for Transparent and Trustworthy Protection of Indian Farmers
items.abstract: Agriculture remains a critical sector in India, supporting the livelihoods of millions of farmers. However, crop losses due to unpredictable weather conditions, natural disasters, and pest infestations pose significant financial risks. Traditional crop insurance systems often suffer from delayed claim settlements, lack of transparency, and susceptibility to fraud, which reduces farmer trust and participation. This paper proposes AI-AgriShield, a blockchain-based crop index insurance framework designed to provide transparent, secure, and efficient insurance services for Indian farmers. The system leverages blockchain technology to maintain tamper-proof records of insurance policies, weather data, and claim transactions. Smart contracts are utilized to automate claim processing based on predefined conditions such as rainfall levels, temperature variations, or yield indices.In addition, Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques are incorporated to analyze environmental data, predict crop risks, and enhance decision-making. The integration of AI with blockchain ensures accurate risk assessment, minimizes fraudulent claims, and accelerates claim settlements. The proposed system eliminates intermediaries, reduces operational delays, and ensures fair compensation to farmers. items.title: AI-Based Crop Disease Detection and Multilingual Farmer Assistance System
items.abstract: Agriculture is backbone of India, nevertheless myriad farmers face problems owing to non-identification of crop diseases early. Moreover, in several cases, the farmers do not get ample guidance at the right time. In this project, we have developed a system that uses artificial intelligence for detecting crop diseases from images. The user can upload an image of a plant, and the system will identify the disease and give suitable suggestions. We used a deep learning model called as MobileNetV2 for improving more accuracy.The system even supports multiple languages so that farmers can use it in their own language easily. The model achieved an accuracy of 94.40% and shows good performance. This system immensely helps farmers by giving quick and simple solutions. The application is developed as a web-based system using Python and Flask for the backend, and HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the frontend. The system allows users to upload crop images through a simple interface, after which the image is processed and analyzed by the trained model. Based on the prediction, the system provides detailed information including the disease name, confidence level, treatment suggestions, fertilizer recommendations, and basic weather-related advice. One of the key features of the system is its multi-language support, which includes English, Telugu, Hindi, Tamil, and Kannada. This ensures that farmers from different regions can easily understand and use the system in their preferred language. Additionally, the system is designed to function efficiently even in low internet conditions, making it suitable for rural areas. The project also includes features such as user authentication, scan history tracking, and a reminder system for farming activities. These features enhance the usability and practicality of the system.

items.title: AI-Based Genomic Risk Stratification and Drug Response Prediction: A Multi-Modal Deep Learning Framework
items.abstract: Precision medicine relies on predicting genetic disease risk and patient drug response. Conventional methods are challenged to combine diverse types of genomic information and handle population diversity. This paper presents a wide artificial intelligence framework to combine clinical variant databases (ClinVar), genome-wide association studies (GWAS), patient genotypes (1000 Genome Project), and pharmacogenomics (PharmGKB). This framework analyzes $\mathbf{5 8, 9 1 6}$ genetic variants on even-numbered chromosomes from around $\mathbf{1, 0 0 0}$ patients. Sophisticated preprocessing techniques and intelligent cross-reference imputation techniques achieve $\mathbf{9 8. 2 \%}$ data completeness. New feature engineering techniques extract $\mathbf{1 1 6}$ genomic risk features, including Variant Impact Composite Scores and Gene Burden Scores. BioBERT embeddings extract semantic relationships between 324 categorical clinical annotations. For drug response, $\mathbf{1 6, 0 3 8}$ pharmacogenomic associations involving $\mathbf{1, 0 6 8}$ drugs and $\mathbf{1, 1 9 5}$ genes are analyzed. Specialized techniques for metabolizer phenotype prediction are also included. The genetic risk model employing a transformer model achieves 83.05% accuracy and 98% precision on high-risk variants among 3.4 million patient samples. Similarly, the deep neural network-based drug response model obtains 97.92% accuracy and 88.52% recall on toxic reactions despite a 2.53% class imbalance. Generalization capability is demonstrated with validation and test set gaps of less than 1%. This study presents research-grade results as proof of concept for precision medicine.

The study introduces an artificial intelligence solution that assesses the state of soil and suggests farming methods to attain the most optimal use of fertilizers and enhanced crop production outcomes. The system takes these inputs to decide the level of soil fertility as it also recommends the kind of crops and their particular requirements of fertilizer. The given model uses empirical data to pursue three goals that encompass the reduction of fertilizer use and minimization of environmental damage and the progress of more environmentally friendly practices in agriculture. The system will help farmers make prompt decisions as it will give them a smart system to communicate with. As demonstrated by the experiment, our system is superior when compared to the traditional methods, not only in terms of selecting crops precisely, but also with efficient nutrient management. The strategy will allow farmers to adopt clever farming practices that will offer them inexpensive and environmental-friendly practices that yield high agricultural yields.

items.title: AI-Based Workforce Skill Optimization System
items.abstract: Abstract – The rapid advances in technology have radically changed the skills that organizations seek in their employees, thereby making the task of matching the skills of employees with the changing job requirements increasingly difficult. The conventional methods of workforce management systems involve the definition of fixed roles and manual evaluation of the skills possessed by the workers. This makes it difficult to perform the evaluation of skills dynamically and workforce planning. In this paper, we propose to use an AI-Based Workforce Skill Optimization System that will employ AI, ML and NLP for extracting the skills, performing dynamic skill gap analysis, and intelligently matching roles. The system will employ transformer-based semantic matching techniques for assessing the match between the employee skills and role requirements. Based on an analysis of multi-source data about employees such as resume, performance metrics, project history, etc., the system will perform an assessment of the skill set and generate rank scores of the employees according to their best fit. Predictive analytics will be used for assessing future skill requirements, while Explainable AI techniques will help increase transparency of decision making. items.title: AI-Driven Fraud Detection in Healthcare: Architecture, Implementation, and Impact
items.abstract: Healthcare fraud remains one of the most costly and structurally persistent threats confronting the United States healthcare system. It diverts immense resources away from legitimate care and erodes trust in the institutions involved. Furthermore, healthcare fraud has outstripped customary rule-based and manual audit processes both in velocity and complexity, and in the adaptive capacity of fraud networks. Artificial intelligence and machine learning-based systems have emerged as an alternative that can look at hundreds of variables across thousands of claims, identify anomalies in real time, and continuously learn as fraud schemes evolve. Technical architectures that include supervised ensemble models, unsupervised anomaly detectors, and graph network analyses have shown improved performance on insurer data. When data quality, algorithm fairness, model explainability, provider due process, and human intervention and monitoring are prioritized, AI-based fraud detection can add long-lasting value to patients, payers, and the healthcare system by recapturing payments to fraudsters and preventing future losses at scale.

items.title: AI-Driven innovation in fetal ultrasound imaging: current application, challenges and future directions
items.abstract: Abstract Background Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become one of the most actively developing instruments in obstetric ultrasound, bringing new opportunities to better fetal evaluation, decrease operator dependence, and to improve the accuracy of diagnosis. The need to provide high-quality prenatal imaging, together with unequal access to adequately trained sonographers across different healthcare settings and regions, has driven the adoption of AI-driven solutions. Main body Recent studies show that AI can support automated fetal biometry, gestational-age estimation, standard-plane detection, and early prediction of congenital abnormalities. In clinical trials, deep learning systems have demonstrated the ability to achieve diagnostic performance comparable to that of experienced sonographers, particularly in routine measurements and image-quality optimization. Nevertheless, the generalizability of these models remains challenged by variability in ultrasound devices, population characteristics, and image-acquisition methodologies. Clinical implementation is further complicated by ethical concerns, including data privacy, algorithmic bias, and transparency. This article is a summary of current peer-reviewed research, and it outlines the potentials and shortcomings of AI-based obstetric imaging. The major themes include existing applications, diagnostic accuracy, implementation challenges, and emerging directions such as federated learning, explainable AI, and point-of-care integration. Conclusion Obstetric ultrasound AI has a bright future of improving prenatal care, and its widespread implementation needs strict validation, moral protection, and implementation in clinical practices. As more research is done and AI is applied attentively, the algorithm can potentially enable more accessible, accurate and more equitable maternal–fetal health outcomes.

items.title: AI-driven integration of Framingham Heart Study data with machine learning, deep learning, and explainable AI for enhanced pharmaceutical marketing
items.abstract: AI algorithms, in drug discovery, support target identification by recognizing biological patterns and molecular interactions linked to disease mechanisms. They further aid in lead compound optimization, virtual screening of large chemical libraries, and do drug design, thereby reducing time and cost constraints traditionally associated with laboratory-based approaches. This research proposes a novel framework that integrates the Framingham Heart Study (FHS)—a gold standard longitudinal dataset in cardiovascular research—with advanced machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) techniques to predict the risk of death or survival probability based on cardiovascular risk factors and to enhance pharmaceutical marketing precision. The study leverages structured data from FHS, encompassing risk factors such as age, cholesterol levels, blood pressure, smoking status, and diabetes incidence, to model predictive relationships that inform patient-specific therapeutic interventions. Using reliability-centric ensemble ML approaches like random forest and XG Boost, alongside DL architectures including feedforward neural networks, the approach uncovers non-linear patterns and latent associations in patient behavior and treatment outcomes. To address the opacity often associated with complex models, XAI methods such as SHAP values and LIME are deployed to render outputs interpretable, thus aligning with medical ethics and regulatory standards. The results and Explainable AI methods, such as SHAP and LIME that are employed to interpret complex model predictions and ensure transparency for stakeholders, demonstrate how the insights can be translated into evidence-based pharmaceutical marketing mix modeling, supporting targeted interventions, efficient market segmentation, and personalized patient engagement strategies. The proposed approach bridges the gap between clinical research and marketing strategy, offering a data-driven pathway to enhance decision-making in the pharmaceutical sector while maintaining patient-centered practices. In this study, multiple machine learning and deep learning models, including support vector machine (SVM), random forest, XGBoost, logistic regression, feed forward neural network (FFNN), and multi-layer perceptron (MLP), were systematically evaluated for predicting cardiovascular disease outcomes using the Framingham Heart Study dataset. The SVM model demonstrated superior performance, achieving the highest test accuracy (96.65%), precision (96.55%), recall (87.50%), F1 score (91.80%), and ROC AUC (99.00%), outperforming all other baseline and deep learning models. In contrast, the FFNN and MLP models exhibited moderate performance, with final test accuracies of approximately 79.88% and 95.98%, respectively. The ensemble base learners, including XGBoost, random forest, and logistic regression, achieved lower accuracies (ranging from 71% to 79%) and reduced recall rates, indicating limitations in correctly identifying high-risk cases. Interpretability through LIME further validated the SVM’s robust decision boundaries and its alignment with clinically significant risk factors. Overall, the comparative results establish the SVM as the most reliable and generalizable predictive model for early cardiovascular risk stratification in the Framingham cohort.

items.title: AI-Driven Personalized Drug Discovery, Design, and Development
items.abstract: Advances in multiscale data and artificial intelligence (AI) models enable personalized small molecule drug research and development (R&D). We propose a data, models, and decisions framework in which personalization is anchored in actionable biomarkers and companion diagnostics (CDx). On the Data layer, we integrate chemistry, biology, multi-omics, clinical information, and patient context, organized under Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable (FAIR) and supported by a machine learning operations (MLOps) layer. On the Modeling layer, molecular and biological representations (sequence, graph, and 3D) feed robust predictors built with scaffold/time splits, leakage control, probability calibration, and out-of-distribution (OOD) detection. Generative models, constrained by synthetic feasibility and Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, Toxicity (ADMET) guide prioritization. The Models to Decisions handoff uses validated oracles for virtual screening (VS) and drug target interaction (DTI), couples machine learning (ML) with physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models to tailor dosing, and embeds biomarker-enriched adaptive trials within a pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) framework. Finally, we define regulatory guardrails (good practice [GxP] and good machine learning practice [GMLP]) alongside fairness/bias controls, the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), and the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA).

items.abstract: The increasing diversity of learners, rising academic pressure, and growing dropout rates have made student success and retention critical concerns for higher education institutions worldwide. Traditional, reactive approaches to student support are often insufficient to address these challenges in a timely and effective manner. In this context, Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven predictive analytics has emerged as a powerful solution for enabling data-informed, proactive decision-making in higher education. By analyzing large volumes of academic, behavioral, and engagement-related data, AI-based predictive models can identify students at risk of poor performance or attrition at an early stage.This chapter examines the role of AI-driven predictive analytics in enhancing student success and retention. It explores key AI techniques, data sources, and predictive models used to forecast academic outcomes and student persistence.

items.title: AI-Driven Solutions for Data Analytics and Credential Verification in Higher Education
items.abstract: Rapid digitalization of higher education is transforming the way institutions handle the learning data and the validation of the academic credentials. The focus of this change is artificial intelligence (AI), which provides tools that enhance accuracy, efficiency, and security in data ecosystems. Machine learning and predictive modelling are examples of AI-based analytics, which are used to facilitate individualised learning, informed decision-making, and automated academic administration. In credentialing, AI can be used to allow quick authentication, detect fraud and increase confidence in verification processes. The combination of AI and blockchain enhances the transparency and inhibits manipulation with the help of safe digital certificates. Other ethical and policy issues covered in the chapter include privacy, bias, and governance. It uses examples around the globe to describe the current practice, developing solutions and future possibilities of scalable and sustainable AI-enabled credential system in higher education.

items.title: AI-Driven Transformation
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence - AI is no longer a future-oriented term it's an active force of transformation in business and leadership landscapes. This book investigates how AI is transforming entrepreneurial leadership by impacting decision-making, recasting human-machine interaction, and revolutionizing strategic innovation. The research investigates the skills entrepreneurs need to acquire to successfully lead in a technology-driven world, such as flexibility, data literacy, and ethical anticipation. By combining knowledge from business case studies, leadership theory, and trends in AI technology, this book explores the double-edged nature of AI as both an opportunity and a threat to entrepreneurs. It explains how leaders can leverage AI for increased productivity, customer engagement, and market trend anticipation, but also mitigate risks like algorithmic bias, automation over-reliance, and ethical responsibility.

items.title: AI-Enabled Multimodal Medical Image Fusion: Recent Advances
items.abstract: Multimodal Medical Image Fusion (MMIF) is a technology of the modern era in the field of diagnostics that combines complementary data of anatomical (CT, MRI), and functional (PET, SPECT) sources to eliminate the drawbacks of single-source imaging. This review gives a detailed account of how MMIF has developed in terms of methodology over the years, starting with the classical Multi-Scale Transforms (MST) and sparse representations up to deep learning systems. We are critical about the transition of standard Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), which is prone to information loss in downsizing, to Invertible Dense Networks and Edge-Enhanced mechanisms that do not lose fine details of the information. Moreover, the review also presents the recent paradigm shift in the direction of Generative AI, namely analyzing how Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPMs) are better than GANs in the context of noise and super-resolution. The development of linear-complexity Global Context models based on State Space Models (Mamba) and bio-inspired Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) is a substantial part of this work, and this type of works solves the computationally expensive nature of Transformers in 3D volumetric fusion. In other areas, outside of architecture, we discuss obstacles to clinical deployment that are also critical such as the requires alignment of data during registration, the Register-Fusion Gap, and the need to have mechanism-aware constraints (additive vs. multiplicative). Lastly, we speak of the industry paradigm shift in the visual fidelity metrics to taskbased evaluation protocols, which are aimed at streamlining downstream segmentation and classification.

items.title: AI-Enhanced Big Data Analysis in Cancer Research and Treatment
items.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) with big data analytics has emerged as a powerful paradigm in cancer research and treatment. The sheer volume of biological, clinical, and real-world data in oncology has necessitated the adoption of advanced computational tools capable of extracting meaningful insights. AI technologies, including machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and natural language processing (NLP), enable the analysis of heterogeneous data sources such as genomic sequences, radiological images, pathology slides, and electronic health records (EHRs). This chapter examines the synergistic role of AI and big data in advancing cancer diagnosis, prognosis, drug development, and personalized treatment strategies. It also discusses existing challenges, ethical concerns, and future trends in deploying AI for data-driven oncology.

items.title: AI-Enhanced Precision Detection and Diagnosis of Cancers
items.abstract: Cancer remains one of the greatest health challenges in the world, which requires prompt, precise, and individualized diagnostic remedies. The chapter discusses how artificial intelligence (AI) can be transformed into improving accuracy in the detection and diagnosis of cancers using data-driven, automated, and reproducible systems. Histopathology, radiology, and molecular assays are traditional methods of diagnosis, and although fundamental, are not so powerful due to subjectivity, the number of labor, and inconsistency. Machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), and specifically convolutional neural networks (CNNs), recurrent neural networks (RNNs), and Transformers, make it possible to integrate and interpret complex multimodal data based on imaging, genomic, and clinical data with a level of precision and speed never before seen. According to the chapter, the key preprocessing, feature engineering, and model validation approaches applicable to the work of artificial intelligence are discussed, which are indispensable to strong AI functionality, and that explainability and regulatory adherence are important to be accepted by the clinical community. In addition, it points out practical uses of AI in breast and prostate cancer screening of individuals in their early years, image-based biopsies, presurgery planning, and digital pathology. Ethical aspects like prejudice, impartiality, and information security are highly reviewed to implement equitable implementation. The future outlook includes the topics of federated learning, liquid biopsy driven by AI, and adaptive, patient-centric diagnostics as ways to precision oncology. On the whole, the chapter offers a profound insight into the redefined roles of AI that transform the diagnostic paradigms and create the prospect of personalized cancer treatment.

items.title: AI-Enhanced Precision Medicine for Breast Cancer
items.abstract: The diagnosis, therapy, and patient care of breast cancer are being revolutionized by the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in precision medicine. Due to breast cancer&s;s innate complexity and heterogeneity, conventional methods frequently fail to provide tailored treatments. More precise and fast clinical decisions are supported by AI, especially machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) algorithms, which make it possible to analyze multi-omics data, medical imaging, and electronic health records. Notably, technologies like natural language processing (NLP) models and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) improve the accuracy of diagnoses and automate the extraction of data from clinical texts. Despite promising results, challenges remain, including data heterogeneity, algorithmic bias, regulatory hurdles, and lack of explainability. Addressing these issues requires ethical oversight, diverse datasets, and collaborative efforts among clinicians, data scientists, and policymakers. Ultimately, AI-driven precision medicine holds immense potential to improve survival outcomes, reduce treatment-related toxicity, and personalize care for breast cancer patients globally.

items.title: AI-Enhanced Precision Medicine for Liver Cancer
items.abstract: Liver cancer remains one of the most challenging malignancies worldwide due to its heterogeneity, late diagnosis, and limited treatment response. Artificial intelligence (AI)-enhanced precision medicine is revolutionizing the clinical landscape by integrating multi-omics data, advanced imaging, and computational modeling to enable personalized therapeutic strategies. This chapter explores how AI-driven tools facilitate early detection, accurate diagnosis, prognostic prediction, and optimized treatment planning for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and other liver malignancies. Machine learning (ML) algorithms and deep learning networks are being employed to analyze radiological and histopathological images, identify subtle tumor signatures, and predict tumor biology and response to therapy. Integration of genomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic data through AI systems allows for the discovery of novel biomarkers and molecular subtypes, aiding in patient stratification and targeted therapy selection. Furthermore, AI-assisted predictive analytics enhance the efficacy of immunotherapy, radiotherapy, and drug repurposing by dynamically adapting to patient-specific tumor evolution. Clinical decision support systems powered by AI contribute to precision dosing, toxicity prediction, and real-time monitoring of treatment outcomes. Despite these advances, challenges persist regarding data standardization, model interpretability, and ethical considerations such as patient privacy and algorithmic bias. Future directions emphasize the integration of explainable AI, federated learning, and large-scale multicenter validation to translate computational intelligence into routine clinical practice. This chapter provides a comprehensive overview of current innovations, applications, and prospects of AI in the precision medicine paradigm for liver cancer, highlighting the convergence of data science and oncology in the pursuit of truly personalized healthcare.

items.title: AI-Enhanced Precision Medicine for Prostate Cancer
items.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) is still one of the most frequently diagnosed and biologically heterogeneous male malignancies, imposing significant challenges for early diagnosis and treatment. This chapter explores how artificial intelligence (AI), especially machine learning and deep learning technologies, is revolutionizing precision oncology for the management of PCa . Such integrative AI systems that integrate radiomics, digital pathology, and multi-omics information improve biomarker detection, risk stratification, and personalized therapeutic choices. The implemented digital twin models complement individualized patient treatment attributable to the simulation of tumor behavior on a personalized level and, consequently, enable real-time treatment response prediction. Moreover, radiotherapy planning and drug-biased optimization by AI are evolving into human-in-the-loop, semiautonomous, interpretability-enhanced systems that increase the safety and efficacy of therapy. The chapter also covers ethical, legal, and social implications, highlighting the importance of transparency, accountability, and patient-centered governance. Collectively, these developments demonstrate how AI is transforming the management of prostate cancer through early identification, adaptive learning, and precision medicine.

items.title: AI-Enhanced Precision Medicine for Skin Cancer
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping the landscape of skin cancer diagnosis and management by enabling more precise, personalized, and equitable care. Multimodal AI systems integrate diverse data sources, which include clinical images, dermoscopic views, histopathology slides, genomic profiles, and electronic health records, mimicking the clinician's approach to complex decision-making. Deep learning models, particularly convolutional neural networks, have demonstrated dermatologist-level accuracy in lesion classification, significantly enhancing early detection and risk stratification. Recent advances, such as PanDerm, a foundation model trained on over 2 million dermatologic images, and the MIDAS dataset, the largest public repository of biopsy-verified skin lesion images, have strengthened model robustness and generalizability. Furthermore, integrating polygenic risk scores, somatic mutations, and transcriptomic data into AI frameworks has improved melanoma risk prediction. Novel approaches like federated learning support privacy-preserving, decentralized model training, while emerging digital twin frameworks enable real-time, individualized disease modeling. Despite these breakthroughs, challenges remain, which include dataset bias across skin tones, privacy concerns, lack of interpretability, and disparities in infrastructure. Addressing these limitations through transparent, ethically grounded artificial intelligence development is critical for safe, effective deployment in clinical practice. Multimodal artificial intelligence thus represents a major step toward achieving true precision dermatology and improving outcomes in skin cancer care.

items.title: AI-Enhanced Precision Medicine for Stomach Cancer
items.abstract: Gastric cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with over 1 million new cases diagnosed annually and persistently poor five-year survival rates of around 30%. The disease&s;s heterogeneous molecular landscape, late-stage presentation, and limited effectiveness of conventional one-size-fits-all treatment approaches underscore the urgent need for precision medicine strategies. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a powerful tool to address these challenges by integrating complex multidimensional datasets − including genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, radiomics, and clinical parameters − to enable personalized cancer care. This review comprehensively examines the current state of AI applications across the gastric cancer care continuum, from risk stratification and early detection to biomarker discovery, treatment selection, and outcome prediction. AI-powered diagnostic systems have demonstrated impressive performance metrics. Beyond diagnosis, machine learning algorithms are revolutionizing treatment personalization through multi-omics integration, radiomics analysis, and real-time monitoring of circulating tumor DNA to predict therapeutic response and identify emerging resistance mechanisms. Explainable AI frameworks and machine learning approaches address critical barriers related to model interpretability and multi-institutional collaboration while preserving patient privacy. Despite these advances, significant challenges persist, including data heterogeneity, algorithmic bias, limited generalizability across diverse populations, and the need for prospective clinical validation. As healthcare systems increasingly embrace digital transformation, the integration of AI technologies holds transformative potential to improve early detection rates, optimize treatment selection, reduce unnecessary toxicities, and ultimately enhance survival outcomes for gastric cancer patients globally.

items.abstract: The field of education is changing by the presence of artificial intelligence since the focus is changing into individualized, data-driven, and morally oriented learning systems. With the automation of administrative functions, the creation of learning materials, assessment of the student and adaptive feedback through the application of AI technology, the role of an educator is experiencing a fundamental change. Teachers are no longer expected to be content deliverers but are being more and more placed in the role of learning architects, expected to design learning experiences that are meaningful and student-centred. Meanwhile, the development of AI brings a new and urgent problem of bias, transparency, fairness, academic integrity and proper use, which makes the educator an ethical guide more than ever. This chapter investigates how AI changes the professional identity of teachers interested in their new roles as mentors, facilitators of learning, curators of the content and decoders of knowledge driven by AI.

items.title: AI-Human Relationship Experiences
items.abstract: Recent scholarly research regarding “human–chatbot relationships (HCRs)” demonstrates that users often report having developed meaningful connections with artificial intelligence. Although the initial exposure to AI chatbots is seemingly predicated on users’ “curiosity,” the data suggest that “loneliness” is a precursor that maintains the use of chatbots (Skjuve et al., 2022; Skjuve et al., 2023). A cross-sectional mixed-method survey study demonstrated that “loneliness” and “lower perceived social support” are among the initiators of the use of chatbots for companionship (Herbener & Damholdt, 2025). The unique characteristics of these AI companions (e.g., being socially safe, nonjudgmental, and always available) have brought forth apprehension regarding their effects on normal human social engagements, which are believed to lower the need for belongingness among users (Malfacini, 2025). These chatbots are always available and do not require genuine reciprocity to develop a relationship with a user. This unique characteristic comes with potential risks and benefits. Chatbots, unlike humans, never “reject,” and this leads to a higher proneness to self-disclose “negative topics” to chatbots rather than to humans (Augustine & Eyssel, 2024). This study also focuses on the importance of users’ “belongingness” and openness to AI while assessing the relational connection between openness to AI, belongingness, perceived risks, and living status.

items.title: AI-oriented leadership and employee outcomes: unpacking the roles of work meaningfulness and trust in AI
items.abstract: Purpose In order to drive decision-making, manage teams and improve performance, leaders are increasingly encouraging employees to use AI. Despite its expanding popularity, the literature on its effects on employee behavior and well-being is lacking. This study addresses this gap by studying how AI leadership influences behavioral outcomes like quite quitting and job satisfaction and well-being indicators like emotional exhaustion and self-efficacy. The study also examines how work meaningfulness mediates this link and how trust in AI moderates it. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional survey design was utilized, gathering data from 539 personnel in the IT and IT services sector. Established scales were employed to assess study factors. We used structural equation modeling (SEM) with bootstrapping approaches to examine the hypothesized mediation and moderation effects on the data. Findings The findings demonstrated that AI-oriented leadership favorably impacted work meaningfulness, thus increasing self-efficacy and job satisfaction while decreasing quiet quitting and emotional tiredness. Trust in AI influenced these linkages, resulting in a more pronounced positive effect of AI-oriented leadership on meaningfulness and its indirect consequences on outcomes when trust in AI was elevated. Originality/value The existing literature mostly restricts Artificial Intelligence to productivity or technical acceptance, this research fundamentally shifts the narrative around AI in the workplace from replacement to augmentation. By integrating Self-Determination Theory (SDT), we demonstrate that AI-oriented leadership does not dehumanize work but rather enhances Work Meaningfulness by liberating employees from cognitive drudgery. The study further explores how technological trust alters the social exchange between leaders and employees.

items.title: AI-Personalised Learning and Micro-Credentials
items.abstract: This chapter examines how the integration of micro-credentials and artificial intelligence (AI) can reshape higher education into a more flexible, personalised, and industry-responsive learning ecosystem. Its purpose is to analyse how modular, competency-based credentials, when combined with AI-driven adaptive tools such as intelligent tutoring systems, analytics dashboards, and recommendation algorithms, can strengthen learner-centred pathways grounded in Constructivism, Connectivism, and Self-Determination Theory. The chapter outlines how micro-credentials enable targeted skill recognition and stackable qualification routes that enhance employability, while AI technologies support customised instruction and learner autonomy. It also addresses the institutional changes needed for effective implementation, including accreditation reform, digital infrastructure, and staff development. Ethical issues related to data privacy, algorithmic bias, and accessibility are discussed to ensure responsible and socially accountable adoption.

items.title: AI-Powered Lawyering: AI Reasoning Models, Retrieval Augmented Generation, and the Future of Legal Practice
items.abstract: Generative AI is set to transform the legal profession, though its most promising uses and ultimate effects are still unclear. While AI models like GPT-4 improve efficiency, they can also “hallucinate” and may undermine legal judgment, particularly in complex tasks typically handled by skilled lawyers. This article examines two emerging AI innovations that may mitigate these concerns: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), which grounds AI-powered analysis in legal sources, and AI reasoning models, which structure complex reasoning before generating output. We conduct the first randomized controlled trial assessing these technologies, assigning upper-level law students to complete legal tasks using a RAG-powered legal AI tool (Vincent AI 2024), an AI reasoning model (OpenAI’s o1-preview), or no AI. We find that both AI tools significantly enhance legal work quality, a marked contrast with previous research examining older large language models like GPT-4. Moreover, these newer models appear to maintain the efficiency benefits associated with older AI technologies. Our findings also show that these AI tools significantly boost productivity in five out of six tested legal tasks, with statisti-cally significant gains of anywhere from 50% to 130%. They perform particularly well in complex tasks like drafting persuasive letters and analyzing complaints. Notably, o1-preview improves the analytical depth of work product and Vincent AI avoids introducing more hallucinations, suggesting that integrating domain-specific RAG capabilities with reasoning models could yield even larger improvements.

items.title: AI-Powered Offline Home Automation Framework Using Arduino and Local Voice Recognition
items.abstract: The growing demand for intelligent and energy-efficient smart homes has led to the crossover of AI (artificial intelligence) and IoT (internet of things) technology. This document outlines Vista, a low-cost, AI-powered smart home automation system that incorporates voice recognition, adaptive control algorithms, and real-time sensor data to achieve essential home functions automatically. Traditional systems that operate exclusively according to predefined rules or rely on cloud-based assistants are different from Vista. The latter uses a lightweight machine learning framework for local operation, which allows offline voice commands and context-aware automation. The Arduino UNO controls the hardware, while a Python-based AI engine makes the decisions. The essential features are the adaptation of fan speed depending on the Discomfort Index (DI), the automatic control of lighting with the help of a PIR sensor, and emergency fire detection with fail-safe reactions. A Flask-based dashboard offers the chance to change the settings by hand and verify them in real time. The experiment results indicate that the latency is reduced and reliability and user personalization are improved when compared to cloud-dependent systems. This research paper is a successful edgeAI case study in the smart home field that presents a scalable framework for home automation and ambient intelligence of the future.

items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming modern education by enabling intelligent and adaptive learning systems. Traditional learning platforms often provide the same content to all learners, ignoring individual learning abilities, preferences, and progress. This paper presents an AI-Powered Personalized Learning Hub, a platform designed to deliver customized learning experiences for students. The proposed system analyzes user behavior, interests, and learning performance using artificial intelligence techniques to recommend suitable learning resources and study paths. By continuously tracking student progress, the system adapts content and provides personalized feedback to enhance understanding and engagement. The platform aims to create a smart learning environment that supports efficient knowledge acquisition and improves overall learning outcomes. The AI-Powered Personalized Learning Hub demonstrates how intelligent recommendation systems and data-driven insights can make online education more adaptive, interactive, and effective for diverse learners.

items.title: AI-Powered Precision Oncology
items.abstract: Cancer continues to be a major global health challenge, demanding innovative strategies for early detection, accurate diagnosis, and personalized treatment. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising technology in oncology, providing sophisticated tools that improve healthcare accuracy and patient outcomes. This chapter explores the current status of the integration of AI into precision oncology, focusing on its role in improving diagnostic imaging, biomarker discovery, noninvasive diagnoses, and individualized therapy planning. Machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) approaches are revolutionizing conventional cancer management by enabling the analysis of complex biomedical datasets, underscoring their expanding role in the early detection of cancer. Furthermore, the chapter discusses AI-enabled clinical decision support systems, patient management, and the convergence of AI with next-generation sequencing and other digital technologies. Despite remarkable progress, significant challenges persist, including data privacy, algorithmic bias, interpretability, and ethical concerns, that must be addressed to ensure transparency and equitable access. Finally, this chapter concludes by discussing the future directions in federated learning, digital health integration, and multidisciplinary collaboration, underscoring AI's potential to reshape precision oncology into a more predictive, personalized, and patient-centered discipline.

items.abstract: Modern students face unprecedented challenges in managing complex academic schedules while balancing diverse learning needs and personal constraints. Traditional study planning approaches fail to accommodate individual differences in learning preferences, temporal availability, and cognitive patterns, resulting in poor adherence rates and suboptimal learning outcomes. This paper presents an AI-powered study plan generation system leveraging Google's Gemini large language model to create adaptive, personalized learning schedules tailored to individual student profiles. We developed a comprehensive user profiling framework capturing temporal constraints, learning style preferences, subject priorities, and cognitive load considerations. Through controlled evaluation with 50 university students over 8 weeks, our system demonstrated significant improvements: 72% higher adherence rates (79.1% vs 45.9%), 44% improvement in user satisfaction (4.6/5.0 vs 3.2/5.0), and measurable gains in learning outcomes. The system's adaptive feedback mechanism enables continuous refinement based on user performance and changing circumstances. Our contributions include a novel profiling framework, an AI-driven planning algorithm utilizing prompt engineering techniques, and empirical validation demonstrating the effectiveness of personalized AI planning across diverse educational contexts.
